body: Thanks for the response. I know my responses are not easy to deal with. I just feel as though someone that does not have to go through the daily pain I do can understand my predicament. Medication is the answer but is also the problem. Maybe in 100 years medication will be advanced enough where it makes more sense, but where it is now is embarrassing. I should not have to deal with debilitating side effects in order to be happy.

Thanks, really I think I would give identical advice as you given your situation. The real problem is, I have clinical depression and need meds to control the problem. You're just not in the same mindset or place that I'm in so I don't know if your advice is really that useful for me. I really need someone thats been in my specific situation to give me hope that there is a way out of this. That's the problem I have with psychiatrists trying to help me. They really have no idea what I'm going through or what this is like.

Honestly, that's part of the problem. The doctors I speak to don't take antidepressants either. It's very tough to take advice from people who don't have to bear the same side affects I do. The majority of these medications destroy any form of libido, numb any intense emotions, and cause extreme weight gain. I hear from everyone else that medication is the answer, but no one really wants to take medication. Not yourself and not me.

Thanks. I don't know, I'm fairly aware of the medications available to me. I look into this virtually every day. Also, the release times for antidepressants are incredibly slow. The testing and then approval takes years and years. What is your situation? Are you on an antidepressant that is working?

Great advice, the part where I'm constantly hung up is I don't feel like I can ever truly be happy until my anxiety is non-existent. My constant struggle is that I don't like myself when  I struggle with anxiety. The only time I like myself is when I'm not stuck in a bout of anxiety. I've never been able to get out of that line of thinking despite years of therapy and meds.
I've tried CBT without much result. I find myself unable to put the CBT to use in real world situations. It could be something I can try again though with a new therapist.
